data.title: Gold Rally Reaches Up Near Top of “Cup” Formation
data.description:
Gold and silver prices have rallied sharply off the recent lows.

While there is no guarantee that this is anything more than a “bounce,” it is of interest to note the price formation on Gold. In particular, the Gold ETF (GLD) which is today’s featured chart.

What makes this chart so interesting is the way that it built a “cup” formation basing pattern. The right side of the cup has been built by the steady, persistent rally.

Price is now approaching the top of the cup formation (resistance). It is likely that we will see some consolidation or pulling back from there. How this takes shape will be important. Bulls want to see consolidation or a minor pullback (that leads to a breakout). BUT if we retrace more that 50 percent of the rally, then we are likely back to the sideways base building again (that will take more time before any breakout).

data.title: Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQ) Nearing Important Retest Of Highs
data.description:

That index is the Nasdaq 100… and in particular, the Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQ).

QQQ is nearing a test of its all-time highs (resistance). A break out to new highs would be bullish, while a failure here could lead to consolidation or a pullback.

data.title: 10-Year US Treasury Bond Yield Testing Upper End Of Range
data.description:
US bond yields are rising again and higher mortgage and auto rates could make consumers a bit uneasy.

And perhaps A LOT uneasy if bond yields break out to the upside.

Today, I share a simple chart highlighting exactly where interest rates are and why this is an important juncture.

Financing is the lifeblood to much of the opportunity that presents itself in our economy. Let’s hope bond yields (interest rates) stall out and fall back into the 3.6 to 4.6 percent range.

data.title: Nvidia’s Stock Price Pullback Tests 200-day Moving Average (Again)
data.description:
One of the most important large cap tech stocks, Nvidia (NVDA) is facing an important test.

No, it is not regarding AI technology or semi chips.

It’s directly related to its stock price action and a key test of psychological and technical support.

Nvidia stock price is testing its 200-day moving average for the second time in the past month. Failure here would likely mean a deeper pullback. But if bulls can support the price again, it could mean the end of the recent pullback. Stay tuned.

data.title: Financial Sector ETF (XLF): Cup (and Maybe Handle) Watch
data.description:
The Financial Sector has been strong for the past 4 months, rallying back to test its 2026 high.

This trading pattern has resulted in a very broad base that resembles a “cup” formation. This is a potentially bullish formation that often leads to a “handle” (cup with handle is the most bullish form of this basing pattern). The handle forms in a consolidation phase.

While there’s not enough price action to say a handle has formed, XLF is testing its highs and a breakout here would be bullish for the sector as well as the broader market.

Not sure if we see some further consolidation resembling a handle, but it’s safe to say that bulls should add XLF to their watch list.

data.title: Retail Sector ETF (XRT) Trading Near Top Of Price Range
data.description:
The performance of the Retail Sector is a nice barometer for the economy. And the Retail Sector ETF (XRT) is currently trading into important price resistance.

This resistance is formed between $89 and 92.50, levels that have been tested 6 times over the past 10 months.

As you can see in today’s featured chart, this level also marks the top of a 10 month price range.

A breakout here would be very bullish for the sector, while offering a bullish data point about the economy. Stay tuned.

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Reaches Important Price Support
data.description:
Nvidia is at the center of the semiconductor / AI movement.

And as AI creeps into the scene, it’s provided some added volatility as investors try to figure out what it means for big name tech stocks like Nvidia.

After a huge run to $200, Nvidia traded sideways between $165 and $200 for nearly 6 months before breaking out on a run up to $236. It then fell back to earth to test a critical price support level (the 200-day moving average).

Nvidia bulls want the 200-day MA to hold. If it doesn’t, it could fall back to the $165 level.

data.title: Treasury Bonds ETF (TLT) Exhaustion Price Candle
data.description:
Interest rates remain elevated as does the U.S. stock market.

That said, higher interest rates translate to downside pressure on treasury bonds.

I write this even though treasury bonds have rallied for much of the past month. But the rally comes off of new lows and within the bottom third of its price construct.

As well, the Treasury Bonds ETF (TLT) put in an exhaustion price candle that could mean the recent rally is coming to an end.

data.title: Financial Sector ETF (XLF): Worrisome to Broader Market?
data.description:
The banks and financial stocks are trading sideways… and well off the highs of the year.

Will the current trading action in the Financial Sector ETF (XLF) prove worrisome for the broader stock market?

The financial sector plays an important role in the stock market so perhaps it is worth taking a look at (or at least considering in your pros/cons allocation).

Today, we look at XLF and highlight its under-performance, as well as a key price resistance level.
